glossary.water reabsorption: Taking water back from the urine into the blood as it passes through the kidney.
glossary.central DI: Another name for cranial DI: too little ADH is made or released by the brain.
glossary.meningitis: Infection and inflammation of the membranes covering the brain and spinal cord.
glossary.sickle cell disease: Inherited haemoglobin disorder making red cells sickle-shaped, causing blockages and organ damage.
glossary.pituitary tumour: A growth, usually benign, in the pituitary gland at the base of the brain.
glossary.lithium toxicity: Harmful effects from lithium building up, often at high blood levels or over long-term use.
glossary.chronic kidney disease: Long-term loss of kidney function lasting more than three months.
glossary.dehydration: Loss of more body water than is taken in.
glossary.gold standard: The most accurate, definitive test for a diagnosis.
glossary.serum osmolality: Concentration of dissolved particles in the blood, normally about 275 to 295 mOsm/kg.
glossary.urine osmolality: Concentration of dissolved particles in urine; low means dilute urine.
glossary.mOsm/kg: Milliosmoles per kilogram of water, the unit of osmolality.
glossary.MRI pituitary: Magnetic resonance scan focused on the pituitary gland and hypothalamus.
glossary.intranasal: Given as a spray or drops into the nose.
glossary.agonist: A drug that binds to a receptor and activates it, copying the natural hormone.
glossary.thiazide diuretic: Drug acting on the distal tubule that increases sodium and water loss in urine.
glossary.chlorthiazide: A thiazide diuretic (also spelt chlorothiazide) used in nephrogenic DI.
glossary.diuretic: A drug that increases urine output.
glossary.low-salt diet: Eating less sodium, which lowers the solute load the kidney must excrete and so reduces urine volume.
glossary.intravascular volume: The volume of fluid inside the blood vessels.
glossary.plasma osmolality: Concentration of dissolved particles in plasma; rises when water is lost.
glossary.volume depletion: Loss of fluid from the circulation and body.
glossary.aquaporin: A channel protein that lets water move across cell membranes.
glossary.trafficking: Movement of proteins such as aquaporin-2 to their working place in the cell membrane.
glossary.downregulate: To reduce the amount or activity of a protein or receptor.
glossary.paradoxical: The opposite of what you would expect.
glossary.inflammatory conditions: Diseases driven by inflammation, such as sarcoidosis, that can damage the hypothalamus or pituitary.
glossary.head injury: Trauma to the head that can damage the hypothalamus or pituitary stalk.
